headline: Elias Lindholm four goal masterpiece leads Bruins to thriller win
morning_brew: I haven't seen a performance like Elias Lindholm put on last night since the glory days. Four goals in one night against the Capitals is absolutely wicked, and it's exactly the kind of offensive outburst we needed after a few inconsistent weeks. The squad looked energized from the opening puck drop, and even when we hit a snag in the second period, it felt like the boys were never gonna let this one slip away. It's a damn shame the C's couldn't match that energy out in Sacramento.

Watching the Celtics lose on a last-second putback is a special kind of misery that I really didn't need to experience on a Saturday night. We had our chances to put the Kings away, but the shooting just went cold when it mattered most, and that's a tough pill to swallow for a team trying to find its rhythm. I'll be staring at the ceiling tonight if they don't pick it up when they head to San Francisco to take on the Warriors at the Chase Center.

Things aren't getting any easier with the Pats still trying to navigate the schedule without Drake Maye. The offense has been a work in progress all year, and until we get some clarity on the injury situation, we're all just hoping for the best. It's a long road ahead for this roster, and honestly, I'm just looking for any sign that the game plan is moving in the right direction.

news_digest.headline: Elias Lindholm authors first four-goal game of career in Bruins' 7-5 victory
news_digest.dans_take: That is how you take over a game and put the entire city on your back for one night.

news_digest.headline: Murray's putback with 5 seconds left lifts Kings to 97-96 win over Celtics
news_digest.dans_take: I watched that final possession through my fingers like a horror movie and it ended exactly how I feared.
